articles.title: Ettore Messina: "El Real Madrid sería competitivo en la NBA si..."
articles.standfirst: El exentrenador se pasa por Otra Ronda en Radio MARCA y responde a la incógnita de si el conjunto blanco podría jugar en Estados Unidos
articles.summary: El exentrenador se pasa por Otra Ronda en Radio MARCA y responde a la incógnita de si el conjunto blanco podría jugar en Estados Unidos
articles.body: Ettore Messina puso el foco en uno de los grandes condicionantes a la hora de medir a los mejores equipos europeos con las franquicias de la NBA: el físico. El entrenador italiano, antiguo técnico del Real Madrid, analizó en ‘Otra Ronda’ de Radio MARCA con Carlos Vicente Gómez las diferencias que existen entre ambos mundos y señaló la profundidad de las plantillas como otro de los factores determinantes. Messina considera que los grandes equipos del baloncesto europeo tienen capacidad para competir en un partido puntual contra una franquicia NBA, especialmente al comienzo de la temporada. “Todos los equipos europeos, sobre todo los más fuertes, pueden jugar un partido contra un equipo NBA. Acostumbrarse y jugarlo bien. Sobre todo, al principio de temporada”, explicó el técnico italiano. La situación cambia, según su análisis, cuando se traslada el escenario a una temporada completa de la NBA. El exigente calendario, con 82 partidos de temporada regular, obliga a disponer de una plantilla con muchos recursos para afrontar el desgaste físico. “A lo largo de la temporada y jugando 82 partidos, hay que acostumbrarse. Y hay que tener una plantilla muy larga, con muchos jugadores que pueden aportar”, apuntó Messina. Más allá de la calidad individual, el entrenador italiano señaló el aspecto físico como una de las principales diferencias entre las dos competiciones. Para Messina, igualar el talento no sería suficiente para afrontar con garantías el ritmo de una temporada NBA. “Sobre todo, hay que igualar el nivel físico, no solo de talento”, destacó. Una cuestión que considera especialmente relevante al comparar a los equipos europeos con las franquicias estadounidenses: “El nivel físico es un tema bastante clave, comparando equipos europeos y equipos NBA”. Las palabras de Messina ponen así el acento en una cuestión que va más allá de la capacidad de los jugadores y apunta directamente a las exigencias estructurales de la NBA: un calendario mucho más extenso, mayor número de partidos y la necesidad de contar con una rotación profunda para mantener el nivel durante toda la temporada.

articles.title: Pedro Martínez: "Debemos dejarnos de excusas y de buscar culpables. Somos un equipo"
articles.standfirst: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la derrota de su equipo, la tercera seguida para abrir la presente edición de la Euroliga
articles.summary: El entrenador del Real Madrid analiza la derrota de su equipo, la tercera seguida para abrir la presente edición de la Euroliga
articles.body: Pedro Martínez, entrenador del Real Madrid, lamentó la mala primera parte de su equipo ante el Hapoel IBI Tel Aviv, que se impuso al conjunto blanco por 102-98, y reconoció que deben "mejorar", tras firmar el peor arranque en la historia del equipo en la Euroliga. El técnico valoró el gran tercer cuarto de sus jugadores, con el que consiguieron remontar un partido que parecía perdido al descanso, aunque lamentó que las rotaciones no mejorasen al equipo en el tramo final. "Dos partes diferentes. La primera mitad mala defensa y como resultado fue una ofensiva lenta, sin ritmo ni circulación de balón, muy mala. La segunda parte, con mejor agresividad, remontamos, pese a que Hapoel es un equipo muy experimentado, incluso llegamos a ganar por un punto", destavó. "En ese momento necesitamos rotar y los cambios no funcionaron. En el último minuto ellos jugaron inteligente, fueron a la línea de personal y ganaron el partido", añadió en la rueda de prensa posterior al duelo. Cuestionado por qué matices del año pasado del Valencia Basket podría implementar a su actual equipo tras firmar el peor arranque del Real Madrid en la competición (0-3 de balance), Martínez apeló a la unión de sus jugadores y al trabajo y el tiempo para "hacerlo mejor". "De poco vale pensar en el pasado. Ahora estamos en otra realidad. Todo es diferente. Necesitamos trabajar juntos, con la mentalidad de mejorar y necesitamos tiempo para hacerlo mejor. Esto pasa por el día a día, por nuestra mentalidad de entender que la situación no es fácil. Pero no solo es eso. Debemos dejarnos de excusas y dejar de buscar culpables. Somos un equipo en las buenas y en las malas; debemos mejorar", finalizó.

articles.title: NBA Insiders Pick Celtics over 76ers as Knicks' Top East Challenger in New Poll from Zach Lowe
articles.summary: While the Philadelphia 76ers built a superteam this offseason by signing LeBron James and acquiring Jaylen Brown, they will have some competition in trying to dethrone the 2026 NBA champion New York Knicks.
articles.body:
While the Philadelphia 76ers built a superteam this offseason by signing LeBron James and acquiring Jaylen Brown, they will have some competition in trying to dethrone the 2026 NBA champion New York Knicks.

NBA insider Zach Lowe said on Thursday's episode of The Zach Lowe Show (5:00 mark) that he polled 30 Eastern Conference coaches and executives on the team besides the Knicks that would most likely represent the East in the 2027 NBA Finals, and they chose the Boston Celtics as the "overwhelming winners of the poll."

"I was actually shocked at the level of optimism for Boston as a Finals team," Lowe said. "... A lot of it was simply based on the fact that they felt safest about Boston, alongside the Knicks, being a top-three seed in the conference when the regular season is over."

Lowe went on to say that there was a three-way tie behind the Celtics between the Sixers, Toronto Raptors and Miami Heat in the poll. The Indiana Pacers finished with the third-most votes.

The Celtics added veterans Paul George and Mitchell Robinson this offseason, the latter of whom defected from the Knicks in free agency. With Jayson Tatum fully recovered from his torn Achilles, he's expected to help lead Boston back to title contention.

It will be exciting to see how things play out when the 2026 NBA season begins later this month, as the East appears deeper than it's ever been with multiple title contenders.

articles.title: Joel Embiid Reacts to LeBron James Saying He Wanted to Help 76ers Star Win NBA Title
articles.summary: New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James has said he wants to be the "final little piece" that helps Joel Embiid win a title and that the big man has "done everything in our league" except win that elusive championship.
articles.body:
New Philadelphia 76ers forward LeBron James has said he wants to be the "final little piece" that helps Joel Embiid win a title and that the big man has "done everything in our league" except win that elusive championship.

Embiid appreciated hearing that from the NBA legend.

"You're talking about one of the greatest players to ever play, if not the greatest. To have him say that, in kinda validates—not so much what I've accomplished, but the way my peers think about me," he told ESPN's Malika Andrews (3:30 mark). "I'm at the point in my career where I just want, I need to win. Between everything that's happened, that would be a good ending for the city of Philadelphia and they deserve it."

Expectations are sky-high in Philadelphia after the offseason additions of James and Jaylen Brown. James' has said that a number of factors contributed to his choice of the Sixers in free agency, from Brown's addition to his friendship with Maxey and the team's championship-caliber roster.

But helping Embiid get over the hump also played a part.

"He's done everything in our league, and the only thing he has not done is win a championship. And I want to try to help him get that first one," he said last week on the Mind the Game podcast. "He has a city on his back. He's been 'The Process' for 10 years, 12 years, however long he's been there. But I think it's time we even get you deeper into The Process. And I hope that I can be, kind of, that final little piece that can help him get over the hump."

There are plenty of questions to answer with this new star-studded Philly team as they look to develop chemistry, establish roles and embrace the challenges and sacrifices that naturally come when several star players join forces.

But the main goal on everybody's mind is simple—win a championship.

articles.title: What's gone wrong at Nike? How the world's sportswear giant lost its mojo
articles.summary: Several self-inflicted mistakes have cost the biggest sportswear brand on the planet in recent years.
articles.body:
It's been a difficult few years for Nike.

The largest sportswear brand on the planet, named after the ancient Greek goddess of victory, has been losing of late. Losing sales, losing customers and losing ground to its rivals.

The one-time industry disruptor is now the establishment and in the middle of a tricky turnaround plan aimed at clinging on to market dominance.

Nike's latest financial results show signs a turnaround strategy put in place by company veteran Elliott Hill, who was coaxed out of retirement two years ago to lead the firm, is working - but the pace of change is more marathon than sprint.

However, its recovery has been dented by the loss of football star Kylian Mbappé, who ended his 20-year association with the brand last week to join fast-growing Swiss rival, On.

The Real Madrid striker's departure raises the question of whether Nike can remain the top logo for not just elite athletes, but also the fans that idolise them.

To be clear, Nike is still a mega brand and popular the world over. But missteps have seen hundreds of billions of dollars wiped off its stock market value as its share price tumbled by 75% over five years.

Last month, Nike was ejected from the S&P 100 stock market index of the biggest blue-chip firms in the US.

So what's gone wrong? And can Hill turn things around?

Matt Powell, a veteran analyst and adviser in the sports retail industry, reckons Nike has made "several strategic errors" which have been difficult to reverse, including cutting ties with retailers to sell only direct to customers online and making limited editions items more available.

"The more broadly available those shoes became, the fewer people were interested," Powell says.

Other self-inflicted wounds he suggests include spending research and development cash on digital operations rather than new products.

"They really shut down their innovation on product. Someone jokingly said they were trying to turn Nike into eBay."

That jibe was aimed at John Donahoe, the former eBay boss behind Nike's online direct-to-consumer sales pivot, before he made way for Hill.

Donahoe's four years at Nike coincided with the company's share price plunge.

His tenure saw sales initially soar, driven by pandemic restrictions that boosted online shopping, but subsequent cost-of-living pressures curbed customer spending.

As demand weakened overseas in key markets like China, Nike announced cost cuts and redundancies.

Its digital distraction allowed newer footwear firms on top of the trends to snap at its heels. Shop shelf space previously occupied by Nike was replaced by brands such as On and Hoka.

This was a stark warning to a company that prided and built itself on innovation.

Nike was the firm that signed a deal with a rookie called Michael Jordan in the mid-1980s at a time when the company wasn't a major player in basketball and still mostly known for its running trainers.

The gamble - spending its entire basketball budget on Jordan before he had even competed in the NBA - made Nike what it is today.

The company built a shoe brand around him - Air Jordan. The red and black colours broke NBA rules, but Nike used it as a marketing stunt and paid the fines.

In years that followed Nike partnered with generational talents Tiger Woods, Serena Williams and Cristiano Ronaldo, who all donned the Swoosh on their way to golf, tennis and football greatness.

While the brand retains partnerships with long-retired Jordan, plus Williams and Ronaldo - Woods ended his association in 2024 .

"[I'm] not saying that what they did wasn't great, but it was in the past," said Tim Derdenger, an academic in marketing and strategy. "It's not the future and it's not the current and that is what drives apparel sales today."

Nike's books still boast top athletes, ranging from Rory McIlory to Vinicius Junior.

However, it has now lost its biggest footballing star in Mbappé, who had been with Nike since he was nine years old, along with World Cup winner Lamine Yamal.

Yamal suggested his move to Adidas gave him the chance to stand out from Nike's star-studded roster, while Mbappé said On would see him "surrounded by innovators who dream of the same things I do".

Derdenger suggests Mbappé's move had parallels to Jordan's decision decades earlier to choose Nike over Converse and Adidas due to the opportunity for the athlete to become synonymous with one brand.

"Athletes have egos and those egos want them to be a part of something big and that they're the ones that are helping drive that change, that growth."

Nike boss Hill said the brand has had "some great moments" with Mbappé over two decades.

"We wish him much success as he makes the move," he said during Nike's earnings call, adding that the brand still has a "great stable of athletes".

For all the "doom and gloom", Nike will stay number one, according to Powell - millions worldwide, including young people, remain loyal - but its mistakes have dented its dominance.

"Will Nike be the gorilla they once were? I don't think so. Can the brand come back to growth and profitability? Yes," Powell says.

"When you shut down innovation, you don't turn it back on and it goes right back to full speed," he adds.

Powell thinks Nike's turnaround plan, called "Sport Offense", will start to show positive signs next year.

Hill said Nike had "more work to do" on its sportswear, Jordan brand and in China as the company announced quarterly revenues of $11bn, which undershot analysts' expectations.

Notably, the company cited "headwinds" in China, where revenue declined by 26%.

Sales of its Jordan brand were also down globally. Hill said the firm had been "oversupplying" the iconic retro shoe and will now reduce the volume and frequency of products under the brand.

Nike said it expected revenues to decline by "high-single digits" in the financial year ahead, adding that it planned to make savings of $2.5bn by 2031, some of which will result in job losses.

Nike's chief financial officer Dave Denton said: "Our results are below both our expectations and our potential, and we are focused on closing this gap."

The company's shares fell by more than 8% in extended trading in New York after the earnings were announced.

Last year the company launched a spin-off campaign to its iconic "Just Do It" slogan aimed at younger generations with the line "Why Do It?"

Young people, and future sporting stars, may ask themselves: Why Nike?

articles.title: Great Family Inspiration: How Bronny James quietly played a surprising role in shaping LeBron James’ final stage of legacy
articles.summary: LeBron James has explained how the Philadelphia 76ers first landed on his radar, and the story starts with his son.
articles.body: LeBron James has explained how the Philadelphia 76ers first landed on his radar, and the story starts with his son. Speaking on his Mind The Game podcast recently, the NBA's all-time leading scorer described how Bronny James' friendship with Tyrese Maxey introduced him to the 76ers guard, years before LeBron signed a two-year deal with Philadelphia in July. It was the first time he had spoken publicly about the move since putting pen to paper, and the answer was not the one most people expected.The decision lands in an unusual spot. LeBron, 41, heads into his 24th season in a new city, while Bronny, who turns 22 this week, stays with the Los Angeles Lakers. Their time as teammates lasted two seasons and produced a handful of NBA firsts. Bronny addressed the split Monday at Lakers media day, and the 76ers visit Los Angeles on Dec. 25.The Bronny James factor behind LeBron James' surprising 76ers moveThe order of events runs opposite to what most people would guess. LeBron did not find Maxey through a front office or a scouting report. He found him through his own kids, and he said so while explaining which factors pulled him toward Philadelphia. Many things went into the choice, and Maxey sat near the top of the list.Back then, neither player had logged an NBA minute. Bronny was a California standout with USC ahead of him, and Maxey was one of the top prospects in Texas, set to play at Kentucky. LeBron said on the podcast that he was close to Bronny first, and that Maxey came into view while spending time with two of his sons. What stuck was how the young guard carried himself around the family. Respect registered first. The work ethic came next, and it kept Maxey in LeBron's thoughts.Maxey, by LeBron's account, has not changed since those days. He told his podcast audience that "this young man now is beyond his years for sure," and he said he was not criticizing anyone who changes along the way. The Klutch Sports connection between the two also played a role, but LeBron placed the beginning of the relationship well before any agency ties.Maxey is only part of the picture, and LeBron treated him as one piece of a roster rather than the whole argument. Joel Embiid and VJ Edgecombe are still on the roster, and the 76ers also brought in Jaylen Brown from the Boston Celtics. Philadelphia could not offer what Cleveland or Miami might have, which is sentiment, since those were LeBron's former stops. It could offer a lineup that fit what he was looking for: a franchise guard he already trusted, a center in Embiid, and a rising teammate in Edgecombe. The two-year length of the deal also suits a player in the closing stretch of his career.Bronny never set out to steer his father anywhere. By the account LeBron gave, a friend simply made an impression on a visiting father. Years later, the same impression became a roster spot in Philadelphia, and Bronny is expected to keep carving out a role with the Lakers on the other coast.Why LeBron James leaving the Lakers was surprising with Bronny James still in Los AngelesLeaving Los Angeles looked like a stretch because of how much the Jameses had built there. The Lakers drafted Bronny 55th overall on June 27, 2024, and on opening night that season, coach J.J. Redick motioned both men off the bench with four minutes left in the second quarter against the Minnesota Timberwolves. They became the first father and son to share an NBA floor in a regular-season game. The Lakers won 110-103. LeBron scored 16 points, and Bronny played 2 minutes and 41 seconds with one rebound. Ken Griffey Sr. and Ken Griffey Jr., who did it in baseball in 1990, watched from courtside."I will never forget that moment," LeBron said afterward.A second came in the spring, when both played in Game 1 of the Lakers' series against the Houston Rockets, the first father-son pair in a playoff game. Los Angeles upset Houston while Luka Doncic and Austin Reaves were hurt, and Bronny logged real minutes next to his father.LeBron James' beef with Stephen A. Smith reveals he's protective of his sonLeBron's protective side has a public record, and it goes back to Bronny's rookie year. On Feb. 28, 2025, he criticized the people who cover and discuss the league day-to-day while answering a question about who should be its face. Days later, in March, he walked toward ESPN's Stephen A. Smith before the fourth quarter of a Lakers win over the New York Knicks for an animated exchange. Both men later confirmed it was about Smith's coverage of Bronny.The roots went back to late January. Smith said on First Take that Bronny belonged in the G League and argued he was in the NBA because of his father. He also appealed to LeBron, as a father, to step in.LeBron answered at length on The Pat McAfee Show, an ESPN program. He said criticism of performance is part of the job, and that he would never stop people from judging how players perform. Personal attacks were the problem. It was his job, he said, to "protect my damn household" and the other players. He also accused Smith of milking the confrontation, likening the media rounds to a Taylor Swift tour.Smith did not back off. On his podcast and on First Take, he said LeBron was misrepresenting his remarks, insisted he had been calling out LeBron and not targeting Bronny, and maintained that the young guard simply was not ready at that point. Each side took shots on separate platforms within a day of the other.The fight played out in the middle of a season. The same Wednesday the McAfee interview aired, the Lakers beat the Indiana Pacers 120-119 on a buzzer-beating tip-in from LeBron.How Bronny James is taking LeBron James' Lakers departureBronny's first extensive comments on the move came Monday, and they were calm. He told reporters at Lakers media day in El Segundo that he is happy for his father and looking forward to playing against him on Christmas. There was no frustration, according to the AP's account, and not much of a conversation beforehand either. Bronny smiled while describing a household where business gets few words."He's got his own path and I've got my own," Bronny said of the decision.Media day itself was the first without LeBron's presence, and Bronny shrugged off the difference. He is entering his third NBA season, still trying to win a rotation spot with the team that drafted him in 2024. The Lakers he returns to are younger than the ones LeBron left. articles.title: LeBron James’ foundation celebrates Akron children reaching new chapter as I PROMISE School students prepare for high school
articles.summary: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has remained focused on his last season in the league with the Philadelphia 76ers.
articles.body: LeBron James, the former Los Angeles Lakers’ icon, has remained focused on his last season in the league with the Philadelphia 76ers. While there have been concerns about how he has been transporting by his private helicopter to the training sessions, his foundation, the LeBron James Family Foundation, has marked a new milestone.LeBron James’ foundation makes an update about a milestone in their children’s lives ahead of the new seasonA few weeks ago, the LeBron James’ Family Foundation’s education wing, I PROMISE School, took to its social media to mark a milestone about their children.The LeBron James’ Family Foundation’s education wing, I PROMISE School, made a post that read as, “From 3rd grade to 8th grade, it’s been a journey full of growth and keeping promises. 💚 We celebrated our 8th grade scholars as they walked across the stage in Hometown Hall for Promotion Day surrounded by their families and IPS community that’s been with them every step of the way. 🥹”The post added, “This isn’t just the end of a chapter, it’s the start of what’s next. articles.title: Victor Wembanyama speaks out against NBA players promoting betting, prediction markets: 'I will never do that'
articles.summary: LeBron James has a Polymarket deal. Giannis Antetokounmpo has a Kalshi deal. Victor Wembanyama has no plans to join them.
articles.body:
Victor Wembanyama has landed a number of high-profile endorsements since making it in the NBA. It appears he has no plans to add betting or prediction market companies to that stable.

Speaking with reporters Thursday, the San Antonio Spurs star was asked if he would consider working with such companies. His answer was an unequivocal no, via Jared Weiss of The Athletic :

"Absolutely not. I will never do that. Honestly, I think it's very sad to see some players promote it. Everybody does whatever they want, but without me."

Wembanyama was then asked how he decides which brands to work with. His answer:

"There was a dimension of money in the past. Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not to my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values. "Obviously, we earn millions and millions, — this is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

"There was a dimension of money in the past. Not anymore. Even if I said that, I've refused plenty, much, much more money than I've made for things that were not to my values. And now, I want to promote things that have a good impact, have a good influence with who I can share messages and values.

"Obviously, we earn millions and millions, — this is not our biggest strength. Our biggest strength is inspiring. I want to inspire in a good way. That's the strongest thing I can do."

The companies Wembanyama does work with include Nike, Louis Vuitton and Fanatics. He's also the cover athlete of Electronic Arts' "NBA 2K27" this year .

A few high-profile deals between NBA stars and gambling/predictions companies have popped up in recent years. Giannis Antetokounmpo is one of the faces of Kalshi, and also owns a stake in a company that regularly sets up markets covering NBA transactions ( sometimes featuring Antetokounmpo ).

LeBron James , who previously worked with DraftKings, recently inked a deal with Polymarket that will pay him $15 million per year , more than he will make from the Philadelphia 76ers this season. Kevin Durant's Boardroom company has a long-standing deal with Fanduel. Nikola Jokic is an ambassador for Superbet, a company in his native Serbia.

This stuff has not escaped the notice of the NBA. League commissioner Adam Silver was asked about the Kalshi-Antetokounmpo deal in February and said his office was looking into it, via Yahoo Sports' Kelly Iko :

"We currently are looking at prediction markets in the same way as sports betting companies. In the case of Giannis, it's a minuscule investment … We need a better handle on all the activity happening out there."

The NBA's collective bargaining agreement does allow players to endorse and invest in sports betting and prediction markets companies like other businesses, they just can't do anything when it comes to specifically gambling on the NBA.

The introduction of legalized sports betting hasn't been without incident for the NBA, most notably with the arrests of then-Miami Heat guard Terry Rozier and Cleveland Cavaliers assistant coach Damon Jones on federal charges related to NBA bets and the lifetime ban of former Toronto Raptors player Jontay Porter . And that's to say nothing of the harassment and threats its players have received from disgruntled bettors, which the NBA joined other leagues in urging action against last month .

articles.title: Jalen Brunson responds to LeBron James’ recent praise
articles.summary: Jalen Brunson responded to praise from LeBron James and Giannis Antetokounmpo after leading the Knicks to their first title since 1973.
articles.body:
LeBron James' praise for Jalen Brunson carries extra weight after the Knicks' historic 2026 championship run. James revealed he once envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden before New York won the title. He singled out Brunson while explaining his decision to join Philadelphia.

Giannis Antetokounmpo also praised Brunson during his own Miami Heat media availability. Brunson responded with appreciation without treating the attention as an endpoint. His comments fit the mindset that has defined his rise. After leading the Knicks to their first championship since 1973, Brunson enters a new season with league-wide respect and a demanding standard.

LeBron James put Brunson at the center of the Knicks' praise

James' comments came during Philadelphia 76ers media day after he explained that New York had been part of his free-agency thinking. He said he envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden, but the Knicks' championship changed that possibility. James chose Philadelphia and said he was happy there.

Even while discussing that scenario, James praised the team New York had built. He called the Knicks an unbelievable team with unbelievable players and specifically praised Brunson as someone he loves and considers unbelievable. The praise came after Brunson's strongest postseason.

The timing also matters because Philadelphia and New York have recent playoff history. The Knicks swept the 76ers in the 2026 Eastern Conference semifinals, winning all four games by an average margin of 22.3 points. James will now face New York twice this season, including Philadelphia's Oct. 20 opener at Madison Square Garden.

Brunson's response shows how he views the attention

Brunson responded to James and Giannis with appreciation, then returned to improvement. He said he really appreciated the comments and respected the two stars, adding that hearing such recognition was a sign of how much he has grown.

Brunson made clear that praise does not change his approach. He said positive and negative attention both have to go through one ear and out the other because players have to keep becoming better versions of themselves or others will pass them. He acknowledged that he still has a lot of work to do.

That response fits Brunson's approach throughout his rise. His path from a second-round pick to a three-time All-Star and three-time All-NBA selection has been built around preparation, toughness, and consistency rather than the idea that he has reached a finished version of his game.

The championship changed the conversation around Brunson

The 2026 postseason gave Brunson his strongest case for league-wide respect. He averaged 28.4 points during New York's 16-3 playoff run and earned both Eastern Conference Finals MVP and NBA Finals MVP honors as the Knicks captured their first championship since 1973.

Brunson was particularly productive against San Antonio. He averaged 32.6 points, 4.6 assists and 4.2 rebounds across 5 Finals games, then scored 45 points in the title-clinching Game 5. His fourth-quarter scoring helped New York overcome a 16-point deficit in the 94-90 victory.

The shift is visible in what Brunson's postseason accomplishment meant for New York. The Knicks did not simply reach the Finals; they won the title while Brunson became the second player in franchise history to win Finals MVP, joining Willis Reed.

Fun fact: Jalen Brunson graduated from Villanova in just 3 years, earning a degree in communications. He still won 2 NCAA championships during that shortened college career.

Brunson's rise explains why the praise feels different now

Brunson's standing changed dramatically after he arrived in New York in 2022. The Knicks signed him after four seasons with Dallas, but his move created questions about whether he could lead a franchise with championship expectations.

Those questions faded as Brunson took on a larger role. He averaged 24 points in his first season with New York, then made three consecutive All-Star teams while earning three All-NBA selections. The 2026 championship confirmed that progression.

His size remains part of the discussion because the Knicks list him at 6-foot-2. His playoff performances showed how he creates advantages through footwork, pace, strength, and touch around the rim. His Finals run added another layer to a career increasingly defined by late-game production.

Brunson's development also changed how New York's offense was built around him. His ability to handle the ball, create his own shot and make plays late in games gave the Knicks a clear offensive centerpiece as the team progressed toward its championship season.

The Knicks now carry a different standard

The attention from James and Giannis arrives as the Knicks begin their first title defense. New York returns most of the championship core, including Brunson, Karl-Anthony Towns, Mikal Bridges and OG Anunoby, while Mitchell Robinson departed for Boston and Andre Drummond joined the frontcourt.

Brunson's health is also part of the immediate picture. He underwent surgery on his left wrist in July after playing through discomfort during the championship run, but he announced Sept. 24 that he was fully cleared. NBA.com reported that he was ready for training camp.

The schedule connects the season to James. Philadelphia visits Madison Square Garden on Oct. 20, bringing James into the building he once envisioned calling home while Brunson enters his first season as the reigning Finals MVP.

Brunson has framed the next step around continued development rather than outside recognition. His response to James and Giannis captured that balance: appreciation for the respect, followed by an acknowledgment that the work remains unfinished.

LeBron James praised Jalen Brunson and the Knicks after revealing he had once envisioned finishing his career at Madison Square Garden.

Giannis Antetokounmpo also praised Brunson, adding to the recognition surrounding the Knicks star.

Brunson said he appreciates the respect but believes he still has significant work ahead.

Brunson enters the season as the reigning NBA Finals MVP after leading New York to its first championship since 1973.

He has been fully cleared after July wrist surgery and is preparing for the Knicks' title defense.

articles.title: Angel Reese's Defensive Player of the Year win looks like WNBA media rewarding its own hype
articles.summary: Angel Reese earned 46 WNBA Defensive Player of the Year votes, but the Atlanta Dream's unchanged 30-14 record raises some serious questions.
articles.body: Atlanta Dream forward Angel Reese deserved consideration for the WNBA’s Defensive Player of the Year award. Her rebounding, effort and ability to force turnovers gave voters plenty of reasons to put her in the conversation. Apparently, putting her in the conversation wasn’t enough. Reese received 46 of the 74 votes for the award announced Thursday. Golden State Valkyries forward Gabby Williams finished second with 20. Las Vegas Aces center A’ja Wilson, the best defender in the WNBA as far as I’m concerned, received four. Four. Reese received more than 11 times as many votes as Wilson and more than twice as many as Williams. The result fits a suspicion I’ve had about Reese’s coverage for a long time: too many members of the media want her to be an elite player so badly that they oversell what she actually does. ESPN TURNS ANGEL REESE’S 49 ‘MEBOUNDS’ INTO PROOF THAT SHE’S A LEGENDARY WNBA REBOUNDER An award decided by sportswriters and broadcasters gives them something convenient to point to when anyone questions that assessment. "Of course she’s elite. Look at the award we gave her." Atlanta was already winning 30 games and playing elite defense The Dream finished 30-14 this season. They ranked third in defensive rating, allowing 103.5 points per 100 possessions. A very good season. But how much better did Atlanta get after adding Reese this past offseason? Last year, the Dream finished... 30-14. The exact same record as this season. Surely the team's defense improved by adding the Defensive Player of the Year, right? Well, not exactly. The Dream ranked second in defensive rating, allowing 98.9 points per 100 possessions in 2025. Atlanta already had one of the league’s best defenses before Reese arrived, and the team was actually a little worse defensively this year. That doesn’t mean Reese made Atlanta worse. Rosters change, opponents change and comparing defensive ratings across seasons requires accounting for many variables. But anyone selling her arrival as a dramatic transformation has to explain why the Dream finished with the same number of wins and a slightly worse defensive rating. Reese helped Atlanta allow a league-low 9.5 second-chance points per game, she averaged an impressive 1.8 steals and she led the league in defensive win shares. But she also joined a 30-win team that already played elite defense. A’ja Wilson deserved a lot more than four votes Wilson gives a defense options that Reese doesn’t provide at the same level. She can protect the basket, switch onto a guard and defend a possession that takes her well away from the paint. Against Indiana in August, Wilson guarded Caitlin Clark with the game on the line in overtime and forced the turnover that set up Chelsea Gray’s winning 3-pointer. Aces coach Becky Hammon said after the game: "I’ll take that matchup … any day." I don't think the Atlanta Dream want Reese trying to defend Clark on the perimeter with the game on the line. In fact, if that matchup happened, it would mean some very poor coaching and execution from the Dream. Reese’s activity around the basket is valuable, but Wilson’s ability to handle that assignment is a major reason she's the league's best defender. Wilson led the league in blocks for the fifth consecutive season, averaging 1.9 blocks per game, while Reese averaged just 0.7. Wilson actually averaged more defensive rebounds per game (7.5) than Reese (7.3), while adding 1.4 steals per game. ANGEL REESE’S LATEST WNBA CONTROVERSY SHOWS HOW VICTIMHOOD BECAME CENTRAL TO HER BRAND The defensive rebounding comparison tends to get lost amid the celebration of Reese’s rebounding records. Of her 521 rebounds this season, 206 came on offense. Those are valuable possessions to create, but they aren’t defensive stops and shouldn't factor into a Defensive Player of the Year conversation. And, of course, there are the "mebounds" Reese gets when she misses a layup and rebounds her own shot. Wilson has advanced statistics supporting her case, too. CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney explained that he voted for Reese while acknowledging that Wilson led the league in defensive VPM, an advanced metric estimating a player’s impact on preventing points. Gabby Williams had a serious argument, too. She regularly took the opponent’s toughest scoring assignment for Golden State’s top-ranked defense. The WNBA’s own awards preview cited Synergy tracking that placed her first in points allowed per possession across tracked play types. Some of the explanations sound a little too eager Consider how Swish Appeal’s Edwin Garcia, an official awards voter, described Reese’s defense. "At the rim, she was a black hole, devouring everything that even attempts to enter the paint," Garcia wrote. He also called her a "shoo-in" for the award. A player averaging fewer than one block per game was supposedly devouring everything near the basket. Protecting the rim involves more than blocking shots, but Garcia’s description makes Reese sound like an overwhelming shot-blocking force. She wasn’t. Garcia also leaned on Atlanta’s defensive on/off numbers, citing a 15.5-point difference with Reese off the floor. CBS Sports’ Jack Maloney used on/off figures, too, but he cited a 13-point gap in his explanation for choosing Reese. Atlanta’s own award announcement said 7.9. That’s an awful lot of confidence in a number that changes considerably depending on where it came from and when it was pulled. And it still measures the performance of five players together, not Reese’s individual defense. ANGEL REESE GOT A BARBIE DOLL, SIGNATURE SHOE AND WNBA THEME NIGHT, THEN PLAYED VICTIM AGAIN Hoops Junkie’s version raises another question. Its defensive on/off comparison puts Aces guard Jackie Young at 15.1 points and A’ja Wilson at 7.0, giving Young a much larger apparent impact on the Aces’ defense. Are we supposed to believe Young is more important to Las Vegas’ defense than Wilson? Watch the Aces play and try making that argument. Young is a good defender, but Wilson is the player protecting the basket, grabbing rebounds and handling assignments most centers couldn’t handle. A number that puts Young so far ahead of Wilson deserves some scrutiny before it becomes the deciding argument for a defensive award. The numbers don’t make Reese the obvious choice SB Nation voter Noa Dalzell cited opponents’ worse shooting numbers with Reese on the floor and wrote: "if Angel Reese is guarding you, your team starts missing shots." Except being on the floor and guarding the shooter are two different things. Reese gets credit in that comparison when a teammate forces a difficult shot or an opponent simply misses an open one. Translating the team’s shooting numbers into a claim about Reese personally shutting down opponents overstates what those numbers establish. Dalzell, like Maloney, acknowledged that Wilson led the league in DVPM and noted that Reese also trailed Gabby Williams and Aliyah Boston in that metric. Two voters openly noted an important individual defensive metric that favored Wilson but decided to push forward using team on/off figures. Unsurprisingly, they leaned more heavily on stats favoring Reese, even if those stats aren't the best barometer for defensive performance. Reese’s on/off advantage is fair game when making her Defensive Player of the Year case. But it doesn’t explain why Wilson barely registered in the voting, or why Williams received fewer than half as many votes as Reese. That’s been my issue with the coverage of Reese for a long time. OUTKICK IS NOW AVAILABLE ON THE FOX NEWS APP: CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD She’s a very good player with limitations that too many people covering her seem determined to overlook. Now, a strong defensive season has become a runaway award victory, and the same media that handed her the trophy can point to it as proof that their assessment was right. It’s a vicious little cycle of self-validation. Reese deserved consideration. But 46 votes to Williams’ 20 and Wilson’s four looks like a media corps that was awfully eager to give itself something to celebrate.

articles.title: 1 Heat player in danger of losing starting job in 2026-27 training camp
articles.summary: No NBA team will add a bigger and better piece to their starting lineup this upcoming season than the Miami Heat. Of course, that is because the team traded...
articles.body:
No NBA team will add a bigger and better piece to their starting lineup this upcoming season than the Miami Heat . Of course, that is because the team traded for Giannis Antetokounmpo, one of the very best players in the NBA . Adding the Greek Freak cost them Tyler Herro, Jaime Jaquez Jr., Kel'el Ware, Kasparas Jakucionis, and a surplus of draft picks.

The former of those departures was not just a starter for the Heat, but an All-Star. The latter three all had experience starting or potential to start in the near future, had it not been for the blockbuster. The point is, the Heat are going to look a whole lot different this season when it comes to their starting lineup. Antetokounmpo joins Bam Adebayo, a fellow megastar who had an 83-point game last season. The Heat will also likely start Andrew Wiggins and Davion Mitchell. The former number one overall pick never quite lived up to his potential, but he has made a productive career for himself. Mitchell is a defensive-minded, pesky player.

As of now, it appears that the fifth starting spot will go to Klay Thompson , another offseason acquisition. However, Thompson's starting spot is at risk.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Who could take Klay Thompson's starting spot?

Klay Thompson is one of the greatest 3-point shooters in NBA history . His 2,899 long ball makes are the fourth most in NBA history. Of course, Thompson's picture-perfect form and catch-and-shoot mastery was at its best when he was one half of the Splash Brothers. Although Thompson has regressed in recent years, it can even be argued that his 3-point shooting has become underrated.

Thompson really is a perfect fit in Miami's starting five because the Heat desperately needed spacing. Antetokounmpo is a downhill player who wants to dominate the painted area, and while Adebayo's 83-point explosion proved he can score outside, he is still an interior player first and foremost. Both players will draw a lot of attention and kick out to an open Thompson. However, it isn't a guarantee that Thompson actually gets the nod as the starting shooting guard.

Tim Hardaway Jr. also has a case to be in the starting five. Hardaway provides loads of beyond the arc shooting, just like Thompson. However, he is a better scorer from the other two levels at this point in their careers. Hardaway can create his own shot, and his defense actually looked improved with the Denver Nuggets last season.

While the Heat have players who get downhill, they actually lack pure playmakers. Miami might be better off with Hardaway's self-creation ability over Thompson's style of player, which relies on few dribbles and receiving plenty of passes.

Most likely, Thompson will, in fact, be a part of the starting lineup. His regression was highlighted buy a recent buyout by the Dallas Mavericks, though, and if the Washington State product doesn't look like his old self, a team in their contention window like the Heat might consider all possibilities, including having Thompson come off the bench.

articles.title: Olivia Miles Talks Being in WNBA MVP Conversations as a Rookie, 'Now I Have to Play at That Level'
articles.summary: Minnesota Lynx star guard Olivia Miles just enjoyed a fantastic season (19.8 PPG, 6.0 APG, 4.7 RPG) that earned her a unanimous WNBA Rookie of the Year honor and even MVP consideration, en route to leading her team to first place in the regular-season standings.
articles.body:
Minnesota Lynx star guard Olivia Miles just enjoyed a fantastic season (19.8 PPG, 6.0 APG, 4.7 RPG) that earned her a unanimous WNBA Rookie of the Year honor and even MVP consideration, en route to leading her team to first place in the regular-season standings.

However, Minnesota's season ended abruptly via a pair of 16-point losses in a two-game sweep in the first round of the playoffs against the New York Liberty. Miles had an uncharacteristically tough series with 8.0 PPG on 20 percent shooting and just two assists overall.

During her exit interview with reporters on Thursday, Miles said she played with a "scarcity mindset" in her first-ever professional postseason experience. Miles also noted that she may have been playing not to lose, rather than being motivated by a "dire" hunger to win.

Live Fever vs. Aces in Must-Win Game 3 ⚔️

Miles was asked about the mindset and why it appeared in the playoffs after not being present in the regular season, and she provided this thoughtful answer (1:58 mark).

"I think it was an interesting year, right? We started off with weird expectations and then we got really good, and then it was like, 'OK, I should win.'

"And then it felt like, if we didn't win, it was the end of the world almost. I was just navigating all those expectations. I also started off as a rookie who no one really thought would do what I did. Now I'm in MVP conversations and now I have to play at that level.

"And it was just like a roller-coaster expectations and emotions the whole year. And I think the playoffs kind of, again, we were playing New York, who probably isn't an eight-seed but was obviously an eight-seed at that point who were really good and at full strength. And so it was a great matchup for us.

"We drop one at home and then, you got to go win on the road. I've never done that as a rookie. Obviously, elimination game. Yeah, I think it was just a lot of stuff going on and maybe I was too focused on the wrong things and things that really didn't matter and should have really just been focused on doing the best I can and just playing carefree in those moments."

Regardless of how the season ended, Miles was sensational and one of the WNBA's best players in year one. She has an incredibly bright future and has every reason to realize it.

Miles had to deal with heavy expectations given her tremendous play and her team's performance, and that may have been a tough burden, especially in the playoffs against an unusually strong No. 8 seed. That would be tough for anyone to handle.

Ultimately, the playoffs (and the season) were a learning experience for Miles, who clearly appears ready to take those lessons, apply them, and springboard into a great sophomore season.

articles.title: Jalen Duren, Pistons Agree to $200M Contract, Latest Rumors on Last-Minute Deal Before Deadline
articles.summary: The Detroit Pistons agreed to a new five-year contract worth $200 million with center Jalen Duren on Thursday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania.
articles.body:
The Detroit Pistons agreed to a new five-year contract worth $200 million with center Jalen Duren on Thursday, according to ESPN's Shams Charania .

Per Charania, the deal is fully guaranteed.

The reported contract comes just before the deadline for restricted free agents to sign a qualifying offer, which is on Thursday at 11:59 p.m. ET.

Detroit's desire to keep Duren was evident prior to the agreement, as Sam Amick and Hunter Patterson of The Athletic previously reported that the team offered him the five-year contract worth $200 million in negotiations.

Still, Duren wasn't present during the Pistons' media day as both sides reportedly remained at a stalemate.

Duren has spent all four years of his NBA career with Detroit after he was selected with the No. 13 overall pick in the 2022 draft.

He showed promise as a rookie before entering a full-time starting role on the Pistons during his second season, averaging 11.4 points and 10.2 rebounds per game across his first two years in the association.

Duren continued to operate as a key starter on Detroit's 2024-25 squad, helping the team compile a 44-38 record and make a playoff appearance after finishing at 14-68 the prior season.

He particularly thrived during the 2025-26 regular season, earning his first All-Star nod.

Duren recorded a career-high 19.5 points to go along with 10.5 rebounds and 2.0 assists per game. He was efficient around the rim last season, shooting 65.0 percent from the field.

The 22-year-old's physicality played an important role in Detroit's ability to slow down opposing offenses, as the team's 108.9 defensive rating ranked No. 2 in the league (via NBA.com ).

While Duren put together an impressive regular season, he struggled throughout the Pistons' playoff run that ended in the second round.

He averaged just 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds per game while connecting on 51.4 percent of his field goals in the postseason, with Detroit occasionally turning to its backup centers in clutch time.

The Pistons still view Duren as one of their core pieces alongside Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson, though.

articles.summary: "Había pensado que me iba a retirar en el Madrid
articles.body: El nuevo Mario Hezonja, alero croata de los Cleveland Cavaliers que cuando llegó al a NBA con 20 años, medía 1,98 metros y pesaba 86 kilos y que con 31 mide 2,06 m. y pesa 118 kg., declaró que "va a echar de menos siempre" al Real Madrid y que quiere "ser una pieza importante para impactar y ser útil para ganar partidos" en su regreso a la NBA. Después de dejar el Real Madrid para volver a la NBA, Mario Hezonja ha regresado a España esta semana para preparar la pretemporada con los Cleveland Cavaliers de James Harden y Donovan Mitchell, en los que espera "ser útil para ganar partidos". "El Madrid me ha dado muchísimo. Especialmente la gente ahí en la sombra que no les ves y les trato como mi familia. Yo los voy a echar de menos siempre, les quiero muchísimo y quiero que tengan muchísimo éxito en la temporada", dijo a los medios de comunicación tras el primer entrenamiento del equipo estadounidense en Fuengirola (Málaga). Hezonja dijo que la salida de Sergio Scariolo del Real Madrid era un cambio que no esperaba, aunque reconoció que Pedro Martínez "es un entrenadorazo" que le "encanta". Señaló que su decisión de salir del club madrileño "no fue por esto... Hemos estado a punto de renovar mi contrato y quitar mi cláusula de salida para la NBA y había pensado que me iba a retirar en el Madrid". "Pero creo que en el Real Madrid estuve 4 años y podría haberme quedado fácilmente otros 10 ó 15 ", apuntó en la jornada anterior. El croata se mostró agradecido al equipo de Cleveland, "que estaba muy respetuoso, muy pendiente todos estos años". "Tuve una oportunidad grande de irme hace un año y medio, pero no quería dejar al Madrid en ese momento tan difícil, en el play-in", agregó. "Individualmente mis cartas están por encima de la mesa. Mi carrera de NBA está en sus manos, en manos de mis compañeros y del staff. Quiero ser una pieza muy importante para impactar, ganar los partidos y ser útil", reivindicó. Se considera "muy versátil" y cree que puede "ayudar muchísimo" porque tiene "muchísima experiencia en altísimo nivel jugando buen baloncesto gracias a estar en Madrid". "Todo lo que necesite el entrenador Kenny Atkinson y mis compañeros, estoy preparado para ayudar", apostilló. Sobre su estado de forma actual para su segunda etapa en la NBA, después de varios años destacando en el baloncesto europeo, dijo que su decisión de salir a Europa fue "para querer dominar, ser mejor y ganar todo", y esto "te ayuda muchísimo a ser el jugador que quieres ser, en la preparación física y mental". "Fui 'drafteado' como un niño, tenía muy poco peso, era todo talento. Pero luego llega el momento donde tienes que hacer muchísimo más. Entonces todos estos años he seguido un programa en mi cabeza que quiero hacer cada verano, donde quiero mejorar de baloncesto, de estado físico, a ver dónde llegamos más", terminó.

articles.title: Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James? Spurs star drops candid reaction after NBA veteran’s eyebrow-raising Polymarket deal
articles.summary: Victor Wembanyama has recently gave his honest reaction to the sports betting debate.
articles.body: Victor Wembanyama has recently gave his honest reaction to the sports betting debate. At Spurs training camp on Thursday, a reporter asked whether the San Antonio center would ever promote a gambling company. "Absolutely not," he replied instantly. He further explained why he is dead set on staying out of it.The reigning Defensive Player of the Year spoke just weeks after LeBron James signed a Polymarket partnership expected to pay him $15 million a year. Wembanyama never mentioned the 76ers star by name but he certainly appears to take aim at the NBA veteran.Did Victor Wembanyama take a shot at LeBron James?Victor Wembanyama was answering a general question about sports betting sponsorships, and he spoke about the practice rather than one player. Asked on Thursday, October 1, he called it "very sad to see some players promote it." Then he added a line with a little edge, everybody does what they want, but without him.For those who have been aware of LeBron James's Polymarket deal, it certainly looks like an apparent slam at James, and the 76ers star is the obvious reference point. The 41-year-old announced a multi-year Polymarket partnership a few weeks ago, and he is expected to earn $15 million a year from it. James also signed a two-year, $8 million contract with Philadelphia this summer. One year of Polymarket money is worth more than that entire deal.Wembanyama explained the reasoning without pointing at anyone. "Obviously, we earn millions and millions," he said, before moving the conversation to influence. A player's biggest strength, according to the Spurs big man, is the ability to inspire, and that can go in a good direction or a bad one. "I want to inspire in a good way."Wembanyama has turned down endorsement offers before when the values behind them did not match. He does sign deals, though. A new Nike agreement includes a signature sneaker line.How other NBA stars have taken betting moneyWembanyama is stepping away from a crowded field. Giannis Antetokounmpo took an equity stake in Kalshi in February, and the Miami Heat star handles promotional work for the prediction market too. Kevin Durant has turned up regularly in FanDuel commercials, and his entertainment network, Boardroom, is partnered with the company. James had a similar arrangement with DraftKings before the Polymarket deal.Betting sponsorships have gone mainstream as the major leagues embrace gambling, and several NBA names now work with betting companies or prediction markets. More current and retired athletes could follow as the industry keeps growing. articles.summary: The WNBA playoff semifinals are nearly set.
articles.body:
The WNBA playoff semifinals are nearly set.

The Las Vegas Aces took down the Indiana Fever on Thursday to secure a spot in the semifinals, and they will take on the winner of the first-round series between the No. 2 Golden State Valkyries and the No. 7 Dallas Wings.

The Minnesota Lynx came into the playoffs as the top seed and were looking to win their first title since 2017, but the No. 8-seeded New York Liberty quickly crushed their dreams, winning the best-of-three series in two games.

Live Fever vs. Aces in Must-Win Game 3 ⚔️

The Atlanta Dream then made light work of the Washington Mystics to set up a matchup with New York.

While the Liberty came in as the bottom seed, it's clear that the 2024 champions are not to be overlooked. Veteran forward Breanna Stewart is the catalyst for New York, and she had a tremendous showing in the first round.

The two-time MVP posted 34 points, 12 boards and six assists in Game 1 before putting up 21 points, five rebounds and four assists in Game 2. She also had a pair of blocks and two steals in both games.

Sabrina Ionescu had a down year by her standards, but she did her job well in the first round, facilitating the offense and hitting shots from behind the arc.

The Dream are one of the WNBA's most complete teams, with two elite scorers in Allisha Gray and Rhyne Howard, a floor general in Jordin Canada and a solid post presence in Angel Reese.

The defending champion Aces may not have finished atop the standings this year, but they might have the strongest case for the best team heading into the semifinals.

Of course, it all starts with the presumed MVP, A'ja Wilson, who posted 38 points in Game 2 and 36 in Game 3. Any team with her on the roster has a chance to win it all.

As for who the Aces will meet in the semifinal, that will be decided on Friday.

articles.title: Caitlin Clark, Sophie Cunningham, A'ja Wilson's Box Score Stats, Highlights as Aces Eliminate Fever
articles.summary: Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson's dominant performance propelled the defending WNBA champions to a 94-83 home win over the No. 6 seed Indiana Fever in Game 3 of their first round playoff series.
articles.body:
Las Vegas Aces center A'ja Wilson's dominant performance propelled the defending WNBA champions to a 94-83 home win over the No. 6 seed Indiana Fever in Game 3 of their first round playoff series.

The No. 3 seed Aces, who were 4.5-point favorites (per FanDuel Sportsbook ), featured four players scoring in double digits.

Here's a look at the game's top performers.

The updated playoff bracket is as follows.

The Aces were up by as many as 10 points in the fourth quarter and then 82-73 with 4:23 left in regulation, but Indiana superstar guard Kelsey Mitchell went on a personal 7-0 run capped by a stepback three with 3:00 remaining to cut the lead to 82-80.

However, the Aces were too strong down the stretch and finished the game on a 12-3 run. Ten of those points were via free throws.

Wilson was a superstar as usual and showcase why she's a lock to win her fifth WNBA MVP award. The Aces were plus-12 with her on the floor, and she also made 12-of-15 free throws. Wilson ended up playing 37 minutes.

Chelsea Gray and Jackie Young played all 40 minutes in this elimination game. Gray, one of the most clutch players in WNBA history, scored 11 points in the fourth quarter. Young capped a fantastic three-game series, averaging 23.3 points, 7.3 assists and 4.7 rebounds.

Las Vegas shot 45 percent from the field, made 8-of-20 threes and hit 28-of-35 free throws. Indiana went to the line 20 times and made 14 free throws.

Indiana guard Caitlin Clark had an up-and-down game. On the plus side, she made a big defensive impact (four blocks, two steals) and scored 18 points. However, she also committed a game-high six turnovers and shot 6-of-18 (3-of-12 from three).

Clark also took an inadvertent elbow to the face from Aces guard Jewell Loyd on a rebound attempt in the fourth quarter. No foul was called.

Overall, Indiana shot just 38 percent from the field and 9-of-32 (28 percent) from three.

Mitchell had a tough shooting night (7-of-23, 3-of-11 from three), but her efforts down the stretch kept Indiana in the game.

Aliyah Boston was arguably Indiana's best player thanks to her 19-point, 10-rebound double-double. Myisha Hines-Allen posted her 12-point, 12-rebound double-double off the bench in just 20 minutes.

Las Vegas will now play the No. 2 seed Golden State Valkyries or the No. 7 seed Dallas Wings in the best-of-five WNBA semifinals, which begin on Sunday.

Golden State will host Dallas in Game 3 of their first-round series on Friday to determine Vegas' opponent.

articles.title: Blazers fire play-by-play broadcaster for racist, misogynistic comments made as a teenager hours after hiring him
articles.summary: The Portland Trail Blazers once again need a new play-by-play announcer.
articles.body:
The Portland Trail Blazers introduced and fired their new play-by-play announcer in the span of a few hours on Thursday, due to social media posts he made as a teenager.

Braiden Bell was announced as the team's new broadcaster Thursday morning. He had previously spent two seasons with the WNBA's Phoenix Mercury as well as various jobs in the college ranks.

Blazers president of business operations Dewayne Hankins was quoted in a release as saying Bell was "a great fit for where we're headed and an important voice for the next chapter of Trail Blazers basketball." The team also teased an appearance by the new hire at their upcoming Fan Fest this weekend.

All of those announcements were taken down by the end of the night, with the Blazers releasing a statement saying they have zero tolerance for "racist, sexist or harmful comments" and that Bell, referred to only as "our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster" had violated that policy.

The Blazers said they were not moving forward with Bell and apologized to their fans.

The Portland Trail Blazers have zero tolerance for racist, sexist, or harmful comments. Social media posts made by our recently announced play-by-play broadcaster are in clear violation of team and league policies, as well as our values and expectations. Therefore, we will not be moving forward with this broadcaster. The play-by-play role carries a long legacy of excellence, on the broadcast and in character, and we hold that standard without exception. We did not meet our own bar in this process, and for that we apologize to Blazers fans and to Rip City. We believe strongly that everyone who is a part of Rip City should feel welcome and safe and we will make sure that our new broadcaster reflects these values. We will do better.

The comments in question appear to be tweets from 2012 and 2013, when Bell would have been in high school. The tweets included statements such as "Asian people piss me off" and "we got a sl** alert on aisle 10."

Bell's X account was made private at some point Thursday. It is unclear what the Blazers will do with the play-by-play spot with preseason set to begin Wednesday and the regular season on Oct. 21.

articles.title: Jalen Duren agrees to re-sign with Detroit for five years, $200 million
articles.summary: Duren and the Pistons may have finally reached a deal, but there are scars that are going to have to heal.
articles.body:
After a summer of drama, Jalen Duren and the Detroit Pistons have agreed to stay together, but scars will remain and need to heal.

Just a couple of hours before the qualifying offer deadline, Duren agreed to the often-reported latest offer from the Pistons of five years, $200 million, reported Shams Charania of ESPN and NBA insider Chris Haynes . The deal is a straight five years, with no team or player options, and is fully guaranteed.

Duren is coming off a breakout season where he averaged 19.5 points and 10.5 rebounds per game and served as the Pistons' defensive anchor in the paint, and with that, he was both an All-Star and All-NBA player. Because he made an All-NBA team, Duren was eligible for up to five years, $287 million. However, Duren cost himself a lot of money when he struggled on both ends of the court during the playoffs — he averaged 10.2 points and 8.5 rebounds per game, had a negative plus/minus, and by the end of the series against the Cavaliers was losing minutes to backup center Paul Reed.

Combine that with the Pistons looking at how the luxury tax aprons are hitting other top teams, and they wanted to keep Duren well below his max. It led to a long summer of drama. Detroit started the summer lowballing Duren with an offer in the low- to mid-$30 million-a-year range, which was tough negotiating by Detroit in a summer when other, less proven centers were getting paid. Duren's ultimate leverage is taking the $9.6 million qualifying offer, and the fact he dragged this out until just a couple of hours before the deadline showed how seriously he considered it.

It may have taken most of the summer, but eventually the Pistons got to a five-year, $200 million offer (and took a ridiculous weight clause off the table). Duren eventually signed the deal.

Now Duren is reunited with Cade Cunningham and Ausar Thompson on a Pistons team that won 60 games last season and wants to take a step forward this season. The Pistons — who also signed Thompson to a five-year, $155 million contract extension this summer — have locked up their core. Now that core has to prove it can take the next step forward.

articles.title: Fever most to blame for crushing Game 3 loss to Aces in WNBA Playoffs
articles.summary: The Indiana Fever came agonizingly close to pulling off another stunning comeback against the Las Vegas Aces. Sadly, their 2026 WNBA playoff run ultimately e...
articles.body:
The Indiana Fever came agonizingly close to pulling off another stunning comeback against the Las Vegas Aces. Sadly, their 2026 WNBA playoff run ultimately ended on Thursday night. Facing the defending champions in a winner-take-all Game 3, Indiana showed enough fight to make Las Vegas sweat. Indiana twice cut the deficit to two points in the fourth quarter before the Aces finally slammed the door. A'ja Wilson delivered another superstar performance with 36 points and 10 rebounds. Chelsea Gray added 23 points, and Jackie Young scored 18 as Las Vegas escaped with a 94-83 victory to eliminate Indiana for the second straight postseason. For the Fever, the painful reality is that the opportunity was there. Against a championship-tested opponent, though, too many possessions went wrong late in the game.

Indiana came out of the gates swinging. They were buoyed by a blistering first-quarter scoring surge from Caitlin Clark that briefly put the defending champions on their heels. However, Las Vegas answered with championship poise. They leaned heavily on an unstoppable 36-point masterclass from Wilson and 23 points from Gray to seize control of the contest. Though Kelsey Mitchell chipped in 23 points and Aliyah Boston battled inside for a gritty double-double of 19 points and 10 rebounds, the Fever's offense went cold down the stretch. Despite cutting the deficit to single digits in the fourth quarter, Indiana simply lacked the scoring depth and defensive stops required to complete the comeback .

When a team builds its identity around a generational floor general, her performance in an elimination game inevitably carries enormous weight. That makes Caitlin Clark 's offensive drop-off one of the biggest reasons Indiana could not finish the job.

Watch sports LIVE with fuboTV (free trial)

Clark actually started brilliantly. She scored 11 points in the first quarter and immediately put pressure on a Las Vegas defense that had dominated the Fever in Game 1. Once the Aces adjusted, though, the superstar guard struggled to maintain that attacking rhythm. She scored only seven points over the remainder of the contest. Clark finished with 18 points while shooting 6-for-18 from the field and 3-for-12 from three-point range.

Las Vegas repeatedly made Clark work for every clean look. After she had shredded the Aces with 27 points and 15 assists in Game 2, the defending champions were determined not to let her dictate the game in the same manner. As such, the Fever's offensive engine lost efficiency.

Clark also committed six turnovers. That further complicated Indiana's attempts to sustain momentum. For the Fever, those empty possessions proved costly. Clark's defensive effort was notable, but Indiana ultimately needed far more offensive production from her.

Indiana received solid contributions from Mitchell and Boston. However, the rest of the rotation could not consistently punish Las Vegas. When Clark's efficiency declined, the Fever needed someone else to completely seize the game. That player never emerged.

Las Vegas could devote greater attention to Indiana's primary creators without fearing enough punishment from elsewhere. Open opportunities became more valuable as the game tightened. Indiana could not consistently convert them.

This was particularly damaging because the Fever had already demonstrated in Game 2 that balanced scoring could overwhelm the Aces. Clark, Mitchell and Boston combined for 75 points in Indiana's 99-89 victory. Clark also produced a historic 15-assist performance. Game 3 demanded a similar collective effort. Instead, Indiana's offensive burden became concentrated once Clark cooled off.

Postseason survival against a powerhouse like Las Vegas requires defensive discipline. Indiana repeatedly allowed the Aces to find their rhythm when the game reached its most important stretches.

Wilson was simply too difficult to contain. After being held to 22 points in Game 2, Wilson responded with 36 points on 11-of-18 shooting while grabbing 10 rebounds. Indiana's frontcourt had no consistent answer. Every successful Las Vegas possession increased the pressure on the Fever's offense to match her.

Gray compounded the problem with 23 points. She repeatedly punished Indiana whenever the Fever needed a defensive stop. The Aces did not need to overwhelm Indiana with one gigantic run. They simply kept finding reliable answers whenever the Fever threatened to regain control.

Indiana actually showed impressive defensive resistance in stretches, particularly when it cut the deficit to two points in the fourth quarter. Howveer, that is also what makes the loss so frustrating. The Fever got close enough to steal the game and then failed to produce the stops that could have completed the comeback.

Indiana's Game 3 loss should not erase the progress made throughout the season. After all, they still pushed the defending champions to a decisive game. Indiana also produced the first playoff victory of Clark's career in Game 2. Still, the series also exposed the gap between being a dangerous postseason team and a true defending champion.

Clark needs to become more resilient when defenses take away her first options. The supporting cast needs to provide greater scoring depth when she is trapped or struggling. And Indiana's defense must find a more reliable formula for containing elite stars such as Wilson. The Fever had their chances in Game 3. They simply could not capitalize on enough of them.
